properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 ships the SHA-1/SHA-2 family; pinned exactly by @ethersproject/sha2@5.7.0 (SHA-256/512 of the ethers v5 chain) and @ethersproject/signing-key@5.7.0 in this lockfile. Available inside the shipped dependency tree of the CLI; no first-party call site (the CLI hashes through ethers v6/@noble). Grover-only exposure; SHA-1 members would be weak if reached, but the CLI never calls this package directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: zksync-cli's own transaction signing: the CLI builds secp256k1 ECDSA wallets from a user-supplied private key (--pk option or masked interactive prompt) via helpers.ts getL2Wallet → new Wallet (zksync-ethers, implemented over @noble/curves), and signs transactions for contract write, bridge deposit/withdraw/finalize and wallet transfer. The curve is fixed by the Ethereum/EVM protocol — replaceable only by a chain hard fork, not by this app, so this is a schedule/monitoring item rather than an in

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 implementation shipped inside @noble/curves@1.2.0, a dependency of ethers@6.7.1 (which itself uses the secp256k1 module). Available in the shipped library; no Ed25519 call site exists in the application code. Changeable only by swapping the ethers dependency stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 provides ECDSA (secp256k1 and other curves) and is pinned by @ethersproject/signing-key@5.7.0 — the ethers v5-era signing-key package present in this lockfile. Available in the shipped dependency tree; the first-party signing path of this CLI goes through ethers v6/zksync-ethers (which use @noble/curves secp256k1), not elliptic. Presence, not direct use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256/secp256r1 available in the shipped library: @noble/curves 1.2.0 ships as the elliptic-curve layer of ethers 6 / zksync-ethers 6.17 (both direct dependencies). No first-party call site found in the application — presence in the shipped build is the inventory fact; the app's actual curve use is secp256k1 (reported separately).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH available in the shipped library (elliptic 6.5.4, transitive dependency of the build). No key-agreement call site found in the application — the CLI performs no ECDH of its own; this is the dependency inventory recording that the capability ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party use: proxy.ts derives the EIP-1967/EIP-1822 proxy implementation and beacon storage slots with ethers keccak256 (keccak256("eip1967.proxy.implementation") - 1, keccak256("eip1967.proxy.beacon") - 1, keccak256("PROXIABLE")). Keccak-256 here is fixed by the EVM/EIP-1967 convention — swapping it would break on-chain compatibility, so it is observable-and-unchangeable from this repo. The same protocol-fixed Keccak-256 also derives Ethereum addresses (helpers.ts computeAddress), reported

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @ethersproject/pbkdf2@5.7.0 — PBKDF2 (HMAC-based) KDF used by ethers v5-era packages: @ethersproject/json-wallets (Web3 secret-storage keystore encryption) and @ethersproject/hdnode (BIP32/BIP39 mnemonic seed derivation), both present in the lockfile. Declared entries only; no first-party call site, but the KDF ships inside the CLI's dependency tree and runs whenever those code paths execute.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the scrypt implementation required by @ethersproject/json-wallets@5.7.0 for Web3 secret-storage (keystore) encryption — the same package that pulls in @ethersproject/pbkdf2 and aes-js. Lockfile entries only; no first-party call site, but it ships and runs in keystore code paths of the dependency tree. Quantum-relevant posture: password KDF, not Shor-breakable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 implementation in @noble/hashes@1.3.2, direct dependency of ethers@6.7.1; used by ethers internally (BIP39 checksums, id(), namehash, keystore paths). Available in the shipped library; the application itself only reaches hashes through ethers (keccak256). Grover-only exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 implementation available in the shipped @noble/hashes@1.3.2 library (ethers@6.7.1 dependency). No BLAKE3 call site found in the application — presence, not use; this records what the shipped library exposes whether or not the CLI calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha3-256 in @noble/hashes as shipped in the lockfile (via ethers 6). Available in the shipped library; no first-party call site found in the application — this is the dependency inventory recording the capability ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the hash-function library this build ships through ethers@6.7.1: provides keccak/SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE2/BLAKE3/ripemd160 plus scrypt and PBKDF2. The application reaches it indirectly through ethers (keccak256) and zksync-ethers. This is the library-level entry; algorithm-level facets are recorded as ALG-928ac765 (SHA-256) and ALG-979eccf8 (BLAKE3).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is the elliptic-curve layer under ethers 6/zksync-ethers 6.17 (direct deps). The application does not import it directly — it is reached through the Wallet/SigningKey wrappers, which is where the CLI's secp256k1 transaction signing actually executes (see the first-party signing finding). The "." site is the root-package dependency record in package-lock.json.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the scrypt implementation the build ships via @ethersproject/json-wallets@5.7.0 (keystore encryption). Library-level entry for the same package as the scrypt algorithm entry ALG-c1f8b585.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

No first-party call site — the application's hashing goes through ethers/@noble; the algorithms ship inside the dependency tree of the installed CLI. Library-level entry; the SHA-family algorithm facet is ALG-50e53f84.
